To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 3D-stacking memory can improve performance by up to 1.75 times, 2) the L2 miss-handling architecture can become a bottleneck, and 3) we can overcome this bottleneck with a scalable L2 miss-handing architecture that combines the Vector Bloom Filter and dynamic MSHR tuning.

3D-Stacking memory directly on top a microprocessor significantly improves performance over commodity 2D memory organizations and the bottleneck shifts from the memory system to the L2 miss handler, which we address with a novel vector data structure and dynamic MSHR tuning.

3D-stacking of DRAM can significantly improve memory system performance and that our scalable L2 MSHA can improve the performance of 3D-stacks even more. 3D-stacked memories have been proposed as a way to improve the performance of multi-core processors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we make use of the additional bandwidth and transistor count provided by 3d-stacked memory to achieve better performance than conventional DRAM?
the design of 3D-stacking memory architectures for multi-core processors and the development of a new scalable L2 MSHR design to handle the high bandwidth of such a memory system.
the design and evaluation of 3D-stacks for multi-core processors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3D-stacking is a very attractive approach for multi-core systems, but it must be combined with a scalable L2 miss handling mechanism to achieve the full benefits of 3D-stacks.
3D stacking of DRAM on a multi-core processor can yield up to 2.4X speedup over commodity 2D-DRAM systems on our memory-intensive workloads.
our proposed 3D-stacking approach, with the addition of a scalable MHA, yields a 2.4x speedup in memory-intensive workloads on a 4-core processor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 3D-stacking of memory and processor die is a promising approach for future microprocessor designs.
we have designed a novel 3D memory architecture and a new MHA that can achieve a total 2.1x performance improvement over previous work.
a 3D-stacking approach can provide a significant performance boost over conventional 2D-stacking approaches, especially when combined with a scalable and efficient L2 miss handling mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the additional transistor budget provided by 3Ds tacking enables us to design more aggressive 3-D DRAM organizations that significantly outperform the more conservative approaches that have been previously proposed.

the 3D-stacking of memory on top of a multi-core processor can significantly reduce the wire delay between the processor and memory and thereby increase the performance of memory-intensive applications.
3D-stacking can be a powerful technique for improving memory performance and that the benefits of 3D-stacks can be significantly enhanced by using aggressive memory organizations.
